bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 59.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content-moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on platforms that host user-generated content.
Online publishers and digital media platforms may face compliance obligations if they host user-generated intimate content.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. It would require websites and apps that host user-generated content to remove such images within 48 hours of being notified by the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to the authority of Congress and the States to regulate contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections and to enact public financing systems for political campaigns.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The amendment would directly regulate how advocacy organizations raise and spend money to influence elections.
The amendment would reshape campaign-finance law and likely generate substantial litigation and compliance work for law firms and lobbying practices.
Regulations on election-related spending could affect advertising revenue and the market for political communications services.
New restrictions on corporate election spending and potential public financing systems could affect financial institutions' political engagement and compliance obligations.

bill.plainSummary: This proposed constitutional amendment would allow Congress and state legislatures to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit them to create public financing systems for campaigns and to treat corporations differently from individual people, including by prohibiting corporations from spending money on elections. The amendment would give lawmakers the authority to write laws implementing these changes.

bill.title: New Era of Preventing End-Stage Kidney Disease Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The bill establishes new training programs and centers of excellence that would operate within hospitals and health systems.
Research into rare kidney disease diagnosis, treatment, and alternatives to dialysis would directly affect medical device and pharmaceutical development in nephrology.
Health professions schools would receive funding to establish fellowship programs and expanded training curricula for kidney disease care.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create federally funded regional centers focused on rare kidney diseases, require certain medical schools to offer fellowships in rare kidney disease care for underserved populations, and expand primary care training programs to include kidney disease education. It also directs the Department of Health and Human Services to study rare kidney disease treatment, dialysis alternatives, and public awareness strategies and report findings to Congress.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys health insurance. People with an illness that is still being studied.

bill.title: CLEAN Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Public Lands, Forests, and Mining. Hearings held.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects geothermal energy developers by increasing lease sale frequency and establishing permit response deadlines.
Electric utilities that generate power from geothermal sources would benefit from increased access to federal leases for development.
The bill involves leasing and drilling on federal land, activities that overlap with mining sector operations and regulatory frameworks.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of the Interior to hold lease sales for geothermal energy development on federal land at least once a year in states where parcels have been nominated, instead of the current requirement of once every two years. It would also require Interior to offer all eligible nominated parcels at each sale and to hold a replacement sale in the same year if a sale is canceled or delayed. The bill sets deadlines for Interior to respond to applications for geothermal drilling permits.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who pays an electricity bill. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.

bill.title: Fight Illicit Pill Presses Act
bill.latestActionText: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates tableting and encapsulating machines used to manufacture pills, imposing new recordkeeping, serial-number, and compliance obligations on equipment suppliers and pharmaceutical manufacturers.
Manufacturers of pill presses, encapsulating machines, and their critical parts face new requirements to affix serial numbers and comply with expanded recordkeeping and reporting rules.
Sellers and distributors of regulated pill-press equipment would be newly subject to recordkeeping and reporting obligations under the Controlled Substances Act.

bill.plainSummary: This bill expands federal regulation of pill-making machines and their parts. It would require anyone who sells or delivers these machines—not just manufacturers and importers—to keep records and report transactions. The bill also mandates permanent serial numbers on the machines and their critical parts (like dies and punches), and makes it a crime to remove those serial numbers or to handle machines whose serial numbers have been tampered with.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
